method.description: Authority capture of the official HTML representations of La. C.Cr.P. arts. 993, 995 and 998, plus controlling art. 986, from the Louisiana State Legislature. Each article was retrieved twice, independently, from the Legislature's own Printable Version endpoint, and art. 993 was additionally retrieved twice from the article page so the two surfaces could be compared. Each response was measured raw, then reduced to operative text by a single deterministic normalizer whose exact procedure is recorded below, and both digests were computed. Nothing was converted, reformatted, deposited or committed.
method.retrievalAgent: curl over HTTPS, Chrome 126 user-agent string, redirects followed, 60s timeout, one process per request with no shared cookie jar
method.temporaryStorage: outside the repository and outside every worktree; not committed and not retained in Git

settledFindingsRelieduponNotReopened: Official issuer: Louisiana State Legislature. There is no issuing forms office; art. 986 makes the statutory text itself the mandatory form.
Official source surfaces: Law.aspx per article and the Legislature's own LawPrint.aspx printable version. Content type text/html on both.
No official PDF, DOCX or fillable binary exists for any of the three articles.
Revisions of record: art. 993 ACTS-2020-73, art. 995 ACTS-2014-145, art. 998 ACTS-2023-342. SOURCE-2026-07-31 is a capture date and is not an issuer revision.
Statewide exclusivity under art. 986(A); the only permitted variation is the court name under art. 986(C).
The Louisiana Supreme Court city and parish packet is non-mandatory, local, and is not a statewide substitute.
Selected output strategy: custom_pleading, from the official HTML source.
Edition 1.3 must retain these three as HTML authority assets under STATES/LA/02_PACKET_FORMS, as their six siblings already are.

captureSurfaceSelection.whySelected: It is the Legislature's own Printable Version of the same article, it carries the identical operative text, and it contains no ASP.NET transport state at all — no __VIEWSTATE, no __EVENTVALIDATION, no __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR, no __PREVIOUSPAGE and no session token. Its DOM is four identified elements: divLaw, LabelName, LabelDocument and, on three of the four articles, WPMainDoc. A raw-response digest taken here cannot drift for a transport reason, which is what makes it usable as a deterministic authority digest.
captureSurfaceSelection.whyRejected: The article page is the full application chrome and carries __VIEWSTATE, __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR, __EVENTVALIDATION and __PREVIOUSPAGE. Its text is identical, so it remains the correct landing page to cite, but its raw bytes are not a safe authority digest — see volatilityAnalysis.

surfaceEquivalenceProved.test: art. 993 normalized text from LawPrint.aspx compared against art. 993 normalized text from Law.aspx, both reduced by the identical normalizer
surfaceEquivalenceProved.result: identical — 7,294 characters on both, byte-for-byte equal after normalization
surfaceEquivalenceProved.conclusion: The printable view is not an abridgement, a summary or a different edition. It is the same operative text with less chrome.

volatilityAnalysis.testPerformed: Each of the four articles was fetched twice from LawPrint.aspx in separate curl processes with no shared cookie jar, and art. 993 twice more from Law.aspx the same way. Raw response bytes were hashed on each run.
volatilityAnalysis.lawPrintResult: Byte-identical across both runs for all four articles. No viewstate is present to vary.
volatilityAnalysis.lawAspxResult: Also byte-identical across both runs today, despite carrying __VIEWSTATE.

correctionToAPriorRecord.priorStatement: It recorded, under method.digestCaveat, that 'legis.la.gov is an ASP.NET WebForms application and every response carries a fresh __VIEWSTATE, so the whole-page digest changes between requests of the same unchanged article.'
correctionToAPriorRecord.whatWasObservedToday: That is too strong and is not borne out. Two independent Law.aspx requests for art. 993 produced identical bytes. The viewstate on these pages is deterministic for an unchanged article with no postback.
correctionToAPriorRecord.whatRemainsTrue: A viewstate is still transport state, not content. Its stability is a property of the current deployment, not a contract: an ASP.NET machine-key rotation, a framework upgrade, the introduction of a ViewStateUserKey or any control-tree change would alter it without one word of the statute changing. A digest that can move for a reason unrelated to the law is the wrong thing to pin.
correctionToAPriorRecord.consequence: The engineering conclusion is unchanged and is now better founded. Capture from LawPrint.aspx, where there is no viewstate to reason about, rather than from Law.aspx with a caveat attached.
correctionToAPriorRecord.correctionScope: This corrects one methodological caveat in the prior record. It does not disturb any identity, revision, role, scope or supersession finding in that record, all of which stand.

A site restyle would move the raw digest without changing the law. That is why the normalized-text digest, not the raw digest, is the value an authority check should compare; the raw digest is recorded as provenance for this exact retrieval.

normalizationProcedure.whyBalancedExtractionMatters: Art. 995 is the exception in this family: its content sits directly inside LabelDocument with no WPMainDoc wrapper, while arts. 986, 993 and 998 nest a WPMainDoc div inside it. controllingArticleCaptured.officialTitle: Art. 986. Forms for the expungement of records
controllingArticleCaptured.whyCaptured: It is the provision that makes the three captured articles mandatory and exclusive statewide, and that limits permitted variation to the court name. It is captured as proof of statewide form treatment, exactly as the assignment requires.
controllingArticleCaptured.isAnAssignedAssetNote: Art. 986 is not one of the three assigned assets and is NOT proposed for retention by this job. Its measurement is recorded as evidence, not as a retention target. No unrelated Louisiana article is added.

operativeTextVerbatim.A: Only the forms provided for in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995, and 998 shall be used for filing motions to expunge a record of an arrest which did not result in a conviction, for the expungement of a record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanor or felony offense, or for an interim motion to expunge a felony offense which resulted in a misdemeanor conviction.
operativeTextVerbatim.B: Supplemental forms may be added to any petition as long as they adhere to the form provided for in Article 993 of this Code.
operativeTextVerbatim.C: The clerk of court for any court in the state of Louisiana having criminal jurisdiction may amend any of the forms provided for in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995, and 998 to provide the appropriate name of the court ordering an expungement of records.

whatItProves: All three captured articles are inside the exclusive list, so their use is mandatory statewide.
The only permitted amendment is the court's name, which is what confines the custom-pleading template's variable surface to caption.courtLine.
Art. 993 governs any supplemental form, which is why the three-Yes/No-section confirmation matters.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The assignment's object is a capture, and the capture succeeded on every axis it set: the official current HTML was retrieved from the issuer for all three assigned articles and for controlling art. 986; volatile transport state is excluded by construction rather than by scrubbing, because the selected surface never carries any; the operative text is preserved exactly; both a stable raw digest and a deterministic normalized-text digest are recorded; the Acts credits confirm the settled revisions with no later amending act; and art. 993's three Yes/No sections are confirmed. What remains is the retention itself, which is Edition 1.3's act and not this job's.
terminalDispositionDetail.notMaterializationRequired: This is deliberately not phrased as a materialization disposition. Materialization is the runtime source pipeline, and under the adjudicated custom_pleading strategy these articles have no runtime binary to materialize. What they need is edition retention as authority of record.

edition13Impact.requiresNewBytesDetail: Yes, and this job supplies the measurement for them. The conditional finding recorded two waves ago became definite when the output strategy was adjudicated to custom_pleading, and the bytes are now identified, measured twice and digested deterministically. Edition 1.3 retains three HTML packet_form assets; this job writes none of them.
